Muscle lactate production increases when oxygen is readily available is not correct; the correct choice is that pyruvate cannot be formed from glucose breakdown, meaning glycolytic flux outpaces mitochondrial pyruvate oxidation. This occurs during high-intensity exercise, hypoxia/ischemia, or impaired mitochondrial function, forcing pyruvate to lactate via lactate dehydrogenase to regenerate NAD+.
CONFIDENCE: 90
